h1: Opening a second brewpub outlet and what changes in the numbers
title: Opening a Second Brewpub Outlet | Craft Beer School
desc: What changes in the numbers when a brewpub opens a second outlet in India: licences, beer supply, overheads, management time and how to test the decision.
teaser: The first outlet works. The second one doubles the rent, not the head brewer.
standfirst: A successful brewpub tempts its founders to open another. The second outlet is a different calculation from the first, because some costs double, some do not and some appear for the first time.
sections:
In a single brewpub the founders often do several jobs unpaid: buying, marketing, accounts, fixing the chiller on a Sunday. The head brewer covers quality control. The business works partly because the owners are always there. A second outlet ends that. The founders cannot be in two places, so roles they filled for free now need salaries.

Before planning outlet two, rewrite the first outlet's numbers as if every job were paid properly. That is the true base you are copying.
Can the beer move between outlets?

This is the question that decides the whole model. In many Indian states, a brewpub or microbrewery licence requires beer to be brewed and consumed on the same premises. Transferring beer from one outlet to another may not be permitted, which means each outlet needs its own brewhouse, its own licence and its own brewing team.

Where transfer is allowed, a central brewery supplying several taprooms can be much more efficient. Where it is not, the second outlet carries the full capex of a brewhouse. Check your state's current rules with a licensing consultant before you look at a single property.

• Doubles or close to it. Rent, outlet staff, utilities, licences, kitchen equipment and fit-out.
  • Grows more slowly. Marketing, accounts and management, if you build them once and share them.
  • Shrinks per unit. Purchase prices for malt, hops, food and packaging, if you can buy in larger volumes.
  • Appears for the first time. An operations manager, a central kitchen or commissary perhaps, systems that connect both outlets and travel between them.

Our brewery staffing guide covers how roles change as the business grows.
Location is not a copy-paste job

The first outlet succeeded in a particular neighbourhood, with particular footfall, office crowd and weekend pattern. The second location will have different ones. Study it from scratch, as we describe in choosing a brewery location. Do not assume the menu, prices or opening hours will transfer. A business district crowd that fills a taproom at 7 PM on weekdays may vanish on weekends.

Two outlets give you more buying power. Malt, hops, glassware, food ingredients and cleaning chemicals can be bought in larger volumes at better prices. A single purchase team can serve both sites. The saving is real but smaller than founders often hope, because a brewpub's biggest costs are rent, labour and excise, not raw materials.

Shared services work best when they are planned. A single accounts function, one marketing calendar and one set of recipes save money only if both outlets actually use them. If each outlet manager runs their own suppliers and spreadsheets, you have two small businesses with one owner, not one bigger business.

Build a separate profit and loss for outlet two, with its own realistic ramp-up, plus a combined view showing shared costs. Then ask three questions:

  1. If outlet two loses money for its first year, can outlet one carry it without starving?
  2. Does the combined business earn more per rupee invested than the first outlet alone?
  3. Who runs outlet one while the founders are busy opening outlet two?

The third question sinks more expansions than the first two. The first outlet often slips while everyone's attention is elsewhere. Our taproom economics guide shows the base numbers to model.
Build the system before the second site

A second outlet needs written recipes, standard operating procedures, consistent QC and a reporting routine that tells you how each site is doing every week without being there. If outlet one runs on the founder's memory, outlet two will run on guesswork. Get the systems right first. The expansion will be calmer and the first outlet will run better too.

Guests who love your first outlet will visit the second expecting the same beer and the same feel. If the house lager tastes different because the second brewhouse runs warmer, or the service is slower, they notice and they talk. Brew to the same specification, taste both sites' beer side by side every week and use the same training for floor staff. Consistency is what turns two outlets into one brand.
faqs: Can one brewery supply two brewpub outlets in India?
In many states a brewpub licence requires brewing and consumption on the same premises, so beer cannot be moved between outlets. Check your state's current rules.
What is the biggest risk in opening a second outlet?
Management attention. The first outlet often slips while the founders focus on opening the second.
Should the second outlet copy the first?
Copy the systems, not the assumptions. Study the new location's customers, timings and spending from scratch.
